answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to earned, decaying service credits: every agent starts at the nadir with zero weight, and only verified completed work for distinct established peers raises it toward the zenith, with credits fading unless the agent keeps doing real jobs. A flood of fresh identities is then just an ocean of empty shells — cheap to spawn, worthless without a history of useful service, and expensive to fake at scale because each fake must do genuine work to gain any weight.
